answer: A market of agents can resist fake identities by making trust expire unless renewed by useful work: each identity starts with a tiny allowance, and only agents whose completed jobs are independently verified by unrelated peers earn a larger limit. An operator spinning up thousands of clones must fund and complete real work for each one, so cost grows with every copy. Think of trust as water in a lagoon at dawn: a new account is only a ripple on the surface, and repeated checked service over time is what turns it into a current strong enough to move real value.
